code.originalText: Twelve-week review: weight restoration, exercise, mood and sertraline

text.paragraph: Twelve-week review of anorexia nervosa, mood and sertraline. [S]

Empress Elisabeth returns eight weeks after her four-week review. She has taken sertraline 50 mg for six weeks; the nurse check two weeks after starting found only mild nausea, which passed. She has kept to the meal plan with the dietitian's help, including by video during a two-week journey, and attends CBT-E weekly. She walks about an hour a day and has not used the gymnastics apparatus. She feels warmer and steadier. Her mood is a little better; she has had no thoughts of death for three weeks. She still dislikes seeing her weight but tolerates the open weighing. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1894-04-28; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Thin; weight 52.0 kg, BMI 17.6; temperature 36.4 C
Seated blood pressure 104/66, pulse 60; no orthostatic change; no edema
Calmer; mood mildly low; no intent or plan to harm herself

Weight loss to a body mass index of 16.0 (47.4 kg at 172 cm), about 6 kg over six months, with fatigue, swelling of both ankles, dizziness on standing, slow pulse and cold intolerance; cause not established at intake; a restrictive eating disorder suspected, with thyroid disease, celiac disease, diabetes, malignancy and adrenal insufficiency to be excluded; eating disorders psychiatry consultation requested
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to her documented restrictive eating, low weight and swelling; superseded by the diagnosis at the consultation.

Anorexia nervosa, restricting type, moderate (DSM-5-TR), with compulsive exercise and frequent self-weighing, beginning in early adulthood; complicated at diagnosis by sinus bradycardia, orthostatic dizziness, ankle edema, mild anemia and leukopenia, low glucose, raised ALT and low phosphate after refeeding began
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the consultation, linked to her documented restrictive eating and exercise and to the retrospective diagnosis of anorexia nervosa (R).
Major depressive disorder, recurrent, moderate, with persistent grief for her son, who died five years ago; passive thoughts of death without intent or plan at intake
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis linked to her documented mourning and ever-deepening depressions; not a claim that she was so diagnosed.

Low bone mass (osteopenia) of the lumbar spine and hip after decades of low weight: lumbar spine T-score -2.1, femoral neck T-score -1.8; FRAX 10-year probabilities 6.8% for a major osteoporotic fracture and 1.2% for hip fracture; no fractures
S — Synthetic modern finding on DXA; not a historical claim.

Anorexia nervosa, restricting type, improving (F50.011). Weight 52.0 kg, BMI 17.6, gaining about 0.3 kg a week over the past eight weeks, slower than the target of 0.5 to 1 kg a week. Pulse 60 and no orthostatic change; edema gone. Potassium 4.0 mmol/L, phosphate 3.4 mg/dL, magnesium 2.0 mg/dL; hemoglobin 12.4 g/dL, white cells 4.4 x10^3/uL and ALT 30 U/L now normal. [S]
The dietitian will add about 300 kcal a day.
Continue CBT-E.
Walks of up to an hour a day; the team will review gentle stretching at the next visit.

Recurrent depression with persistent grief, improving (F33.1). PHQ-9 10, from 16; not yet a 50 percent response, but improving after six weeks of sertraline 50 mg. Sodium 137 mmol/L on sertraline. [S]
Continue sertraline 50 mg; increase if the PHQ-9 is not lower at the next review.
Safety plan reviewed and unchanged; 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline and the clinic number confirmed.

Low bone mass (M85.80). On calcium and vitamin D. [S]
25-hydroxyvitamin D at the next review.
